detail.longDescription:
Like everyone else, I’ve been looking for a good mesh VPN solution and I finally
found Nebula [https://nebula.defined.net/docs/]. Apparently it was created by
Slack and later open sourced. I don’t know people don’t talk about it more.
Pros: - really easy to self host - clear logs make it easier to troubleshoot
then other options - free Android app (as it it doesn’t require subscription)
Cons: - setup is quite manual - doesn’t offer DNS (I just deployed PiHole
instance) (there’s Nebula Commander [https://nebulacommander.com/] that should
make the setup easier but I haven’t tried it). You basically create one node
accessible to all the other nodes. In my case I have to expose a single port to
the internet. Then you manually create private keys and distribute them to
servers. With a bit of configuration you setup the firewall, routing and relays.
And you really only need a bit of configuration. I only had to connect about 5
devices so it was totally doable by hand (i.e. without commander). Before that I
tried: - headscale - didn’t work for some reason. apparently setting it behind
reverse proxy is not officially supported and it requires port 443 so I would
need to setup a dedicates server for it - Netbird - it was working fine on
severs but I got tired of the battery drain issue on Android - Netmaker - too
many functions are locked behind the subscription. Android app doesn’t work with
free accounts and WG setup didn’t work for me I didn’t try Tailscale because I
wanted something I can self host (and headscale didn’t work for me) So if you
don’t have too many nodes and are looking for something easy to self host I
totally recommend Nebula.
